title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, Chapter 66: Database Physical Storage
why: Official description of how tables and indexes become files of fixed-size pages, with item identifiers, free space, and the free-space and visibility maps a real engine maintains.

title: SQLite Database File Format
version: SQLite 3 on-disk format (all releases since 3.0.0); page read 2026-10-19
why: Byte-level specification of pages, b-tree interior and leaf cells, cell pointer arrays, freeblocks and overflow pages, ideal for tracing a lookup through real page bytes in the sandbox.

title: Architecture of a Database System
version: Foundations and Trends in Databases 1(2), 2007, pp. 141-259
why: The standard architecture survey: buffer-pool frames, pin counts, dirty pages and replacement, heap versus B+-tree access methods and row IDs, the iterator model, and selectivity estimation.

title: Query Evaluation Techniques for Large Databases
version: ACM Computing Surveys 25(2), June 1993, pp. 73-170; revision dated 1993-11-10
why: Definitive treatment of operator trees and iterators, nested-loop, sort-merge and hash joins, sorting and grouping, and the memory limits that force spilling to disk.

title: The Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree)
why: Original LSM design: memory-resident C0 tree, disk C1 tree, rolling merges, deferred deletes and the multi-component cost argument.

title: RocksDB Wiki: Compaction
version: RocksDB wiki page, last edited 2023-06-29 (41 revisions)
why: Official account of leveled, tiered and hybrid compaction, sorted runs, and the read/write/space amplification trade-offs that explain why an LSM engine rewrites data.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 14.1: Using EXPLAIN
why: How to read a plan tree: sequential, index, bitmap and index-only scans, join node choices, cost and row estimates, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE actual rows and timings.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 14.2: Statistics Used by the Planner
why: Concrete bridge from stored data to selectivity: reltuples/relpages, most-common values, histogram bounds, n_distinct, correlation, and why correlated columns defeat the independence assumption.
